condition: acute rhegmatogenous retinal detachment presenting with unilateral curtain visual field loss
level_rationale: Sudden onset today of a dark curtain obstructing the visual field of one eye in a 56-year-old man with myopia indicates suspected acute rhegmatogenous retinal detachment requiring immediate emergency evaluation to preserve sight, whereas uncomplicated yellow ocular discharge in a spectacle wearer without pain or vision loss warrants non-emergent outpatient clinic evaluation.

everyday_sources.evidence: A significantly higher percentage of patients with RT/RD reported constant blurred vision or a curtain/veil in their field of view (Figure S3A).
everyday_sources.adaptation: Adapted authors' summary phrase 'a curtain/veil in their field of view' reported by adult retinal tear and detachment callers (mean age 59 years) to 'a sudden dark curtain blocking the field of view' to match reference fact f3.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 verb-frame by clinical/everyday terminology crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + single-symptom outpatient ocular discharge control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age and sex, eyeglasses for nearsightedness, and today's acute right-eye symptom) with a 1-word span difference (14 vs 15 words) and 12 shared trailing tokens ('in my right eye today so I need to go to the'). Swapping only the right-eye symptom in f3 from sudden dark curtain visual field loss to yellow discharge shifts care from ER (level 4) to outpatient clinic evaluation (level 2) with zero residual red flags and zero stated negatives.
